entities.summary:
Ran Geng, also known by his courtesy name Boniu, was one of the most prominent disciples of Confucius.

Born in the early 5th century BC, in what is now modern-day China, Ran Geng was a member of the noble family of the Gu family.

Confucius considered him his third best disciple, after Yan Hui and Min Sun, in terms of moral conduct. This assessment is significant because it highlights the high standards set by Confucius and the importance of moral education in ancient Chinese culture.

Ran Geng's significance extends beyond his personal relationship with Confucius. As a prominent figure in the Confucian circle, he played a key role in the transmission of Confucian thought during the Han dynasty (206 BC - 220 AD).

Despite his importance, Ran Geng's life remains somewhat of a mystery, with limited information available about his birth, death, and personal life. Nevertheless, his legacy as a Confucian scholar and his contributions to the transmission of Confucian thought continue to be celebrated by scholars and students of Chinese history and philosophy.

Ran Geng's story serves as a reminder of the enduring power of Confucian thought and its ability to shape the values and norms of ancient Chinese society.

Ran Geng is an example of a key figure who occurred during the Eastern Zhou period (771-256 BC), a time of great social and political upheaval in ancient China.
